item.description: Hey ^^ This is the new version, as the old one was not clear in certain aspects.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: My design is meant to be spooky, but I may not achieve this factor.

Page Layout: The usual SCP statements, Item Name, Item Class but no picture. Information is going to be structured in the following layout; Appearance description (Height, weight, colour and shape), Discovery (How the anomaly was contained), Abilities (What the anomaly can do, how it does it etc) and the Addendums (Stories about previously explained things).

Elevator Pitch: The basic premise is a tall, slender, arctic hunter with elongated shoulder growths and large elbows, glowing crimson eyes, capable of seeing infrared radiation and heat signature, used for hunting. The anomaly has thousands of tiny muscles on its skin capable of moving guanine crystals to adjust the wavelength of light being reflected off the skin of the anomaly. This is commonly known as camouflage, and is the same method that the Chamaeleonidae (Common Chameleon) uses. Bone marrow scans and nervous axon scans have suggested that overgrowths on the anomaly's shoulder blades and elbows contain many nerve endings, which transfer electrical signals in large amounts to a particular area which creates an electromagnetic field. These electromagnetic pulses disrupt nearby local electric signals. It may use this to alter the function of electrical signals in the brain, or to inhibit power of technology.

Central Narrative: It was a normal day in the UK Arctic Research Facility. It was collection day, where the scientific staff would take a collection of snow for carbon-testing, a process where the amount of carbon that is in a snowflake is collected. Suddenly, the power went out. As the staff stumbled over to the generator, senior researcher Noel Leon noticed a small red glow. Must have been nothing. He got back to fixing the generator and replaced the fuses. But as soon as the generator start-up was initiated, the generator failed. What was going on? Suddenly, pat… pat… pat…. He turned around, but there was nothing but footprints. SNAP. The crunch of his bones in SCP-XXXX's mouth was horrifying, but unheard to remaining staff. As it entered the facility, seven of it's prey had already been frozen. An easy meal. Junior researcher Doctor Edward turned a corner, but the anomaly was gone, just a frozen, half-eaten corpse. He was petrified, and sprinted out to the door and locked it shut. His frozen fingers dialled 911 into a telephone. The rest of the facility was wiped out, with the exception of Doctor Bradly who was obliterated by SCP-XXXX. Doctor Bradly called local authorities and the foundation was alerted. MTF unit Delta-92 Snow-and-Tell was sent to the situation immediately. Using infrared vision, the anomaly's ability was stunted, rendering it useless. Using a Class-3 collapsible containment cell, SCP-XXXX was taken to Site-25 via helicopter with ease.

Welcome the 1930s. item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a human-like creature, around 6 feet tall. This is a SCP that is impossible to look at-not in the way of SCP-096 where if you look at its face, it will kill you, but as in the body will do everything it can to force a person not to look at it, e.g. making the person close their eyes, turning their head away, etc., similar to agnosia-this also effects photos and video recordings, not doing anything to alter them but still having the agnosia-type effect. The SCP is malevolent, and seems to be conscious of the effect it causes, as it constantly uses its inability to not be seen to anyone in the foundation to attempt escapes very frequently, making the containment not impossible, but very, very difficult.

Central Narrative: The foundation traces this SCP back to a road in an undisclosed town in Ohio, as specific section of the road had a sharp increase of traffic accidents for no apparent reason within 2-3 hours. After an investigative team gets there, they find nothing out of the ordinary except that they are physically unable to look down the center of the road. after pinpointing the center of the anomaly, they manage to find that the source of it is said SCP. The SCP goes along willingly, as this is its first encounter with the Foundation, but its anger towards them quickly ratchets up as strict containment procedures limit its freedom.

Item #: SCP-5232

Object Class: Safe

Threat Level: Blue

Special Containment Procedures: [All information regarding SCP-5170 is to be hidden from level 1 personnel or less if a person of such level accesses information regarding SCP-5170 they are to immediately receive Class-B Amnestics. SCP-5232 is to be kept in a 30m2 cell and protocol 202-5232-A

Protocol 202-5232-A forbids any foundation personnel to enter the cell unless they have already come within 30m of this SCP before the protocol was in place, tests with D-CLASS on SCP-5232 is still allowed as long as as the test is done by a level 3 or higher researcher.

Any cleaning of SCP-5232's cell is to be done by a D-CLASS janitor or any janitor who has come in contact with SCP-5232 beforehand and survived.

It has also been concluded impossible to destroy SCP-5232 and impossible to stop it rolling.

Description: [SCP-5232 is a six-sided silver dice of unknown origin. SCP-5232 does not show any anomalies properties until an entity (human, animal, plant and SCP all included) comes within 30m2 of the SCP, if an entity comes within 30m2 the dice will then proceed to roll itself, which tests have shown is completely randomized.

Once it has done this, if the higher value the number value displayed on the top of the dice, the higher level of damage the entity suffers. Tests show there is no way to cancel the anomalous effects and tests show the type of damage/death the entity suffers is also randomized. Also, a roll of one so far appears to guarantee no damage and a roll of six so far appears to guarantee instant death.]

Researcher: [Nadiva Raghe]

Researcher 2: [Very well, starting a new log]

Researcher: [Dr Nadiva Raghe]

CLASS-D: [As you wish.]

<End Log, [12:21]>

However, more tests are required to prove that theory. It must also be noted that the security guard who tranquillized D-4546E had previously come in contact with SCP-5232 and had survived with only a broken leg as a casualty]

CLASS-D group: [D-4546F, D-4546G, D-4546H, D-4546I and D-4546K]

Researcher: [Dr Nadiva Raghe]

D-4546G: [Seems that way Dr.]

Researcher: [Security please can you come in and escort D-4546H to a medical team and D-4546I to receive Class-B Amnestics, thank you]

Researcher: [The two of you that entered last please leave the cell and wait outside the door.]

D-4546G: [That would be me and D-4546F Dr. Should I leave the camera with D-4546K?]

D-4546K: [Its rolled a 2, same as D-4546I]

Researcher: [Interesting, D-4546K please check your left shoulder for a scratch mark.]

D-4546K: [No scratch mark Dr, however, I think my ankle is sprained]

Researcher: [Ok so it seems even though the dice can roll the same value the effect is different. D-4546K: Casualties: Sprained ankle.]

D-4546K: [Dr the dice is rolling again although I am the only one in the room.]

Researcher: [Please can you get D-4546G and D-4546F back in the cell.]

item.title: Killbox & Co.
item.description: A used car lot offering cars that kill their drivers.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): Description with interviews and a mission log

Elevator Pitch: A used car lot in Colorado that offers dirt-cheap classic autos. All owners crash fatally after a week of driving.

Central Narrative:
+ My first custom block
- Are you proud of me ma

The Foundation notices an absurdly sharp increase in automotive-related deaths tracing back to a single car lot and, after some investigating, designate it an anomaly, including all staff. Interview logs with staff members. Staff members don't require sustenance and at 10 pm sharp are all in their designated spot, sleeping. The next day their memory is reset. When talked to, they generally behave like normal humans and show very strong devotion to the car lot. Surveilance instated in a garage which provides the lot with its cars - proved futile as when a car appears, recording equipment malfunctions and witnesses black out. If anyone is seen approaching the garage, a staff member will warn them against it and become more and more agitated if subject doesn't move or refuse. Additionaly, other staff will begin to converge. If subject continues towards garage, staff will apprehend and throw them out. If subject gets into the garage, the salesman will say "Looks like the boss will take care of you now", upon which all exits to the garage close and Mr. Killbox enters the garage through a door leading to the main building. He is a 2.5 m brute with a mechanical arm made out of car parts. Shall the subject be caught, he will be killed and dragged behind the same door, which opens to an empty void for Killbox.
The staff will also start acting hostile if subject mentions Killbox by name or starts asking multiple questions in a row regarding the garage or the cars' origins.
Questions asked about the workers or the car lot will generally all result in answers like "The car lot is my life" and "I've worked here since as long as I can remember."
Staff have realistic human personalities, showing emotions and reacting as to be expected from regular humans. Their daily memory reset generally prevents them from developing critical thoughts. However, they are still capable of thinking freely (save for the instinctual response to trespassing into the garage).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Final Destination-style elaborate death setups.

Additional Notes: Crashes aim to also kill bystanders. Spectacularly. Hence the death toll.

item.title: SCP idea - The Choir of Lamentation // Greenlights and feedbacks needed
item.description: An omnious choir of voices heard throughout the Foundation's locations
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional

Page Layout: Classic, I guess (Name, Class, Procedures, Description and additional logs)

Elevator Pitch: The Choir of Lamentation or Lamentation is a Safe SCP, it is harmless for it has no physical form, it is basically just an auditory phenomenon, but the Foundation still can't understand how it's triggered, as it doesn't have a fix location, nor seems to have a pattern for its manifestations. In my mind, it actually is the expression of the deepest sadness and anger SCPs and personnel alike might have experienced because of the Foundation. The file refers to different events by naming Sites (like the one where A Hero is Born is contained, or the Soup Bowl), and reporting lyrics sung by the Choir, giving hints it narrates other SCPs stories (important details being censored so they can't be identified by the general eyes, but I'd add in footnotes cross-links of hypothesis) such as Playland (and Hailey's disappearance, which destroyed her father), the all-knowing robot lady from 1866 (and her unavoidable loneliness), the events of SCP-1530-2 and -3 recovery (and the death of their mistress, another anomaly), or Timmi's heartbreaking tale.

Central Narrative: It would be a very short article (About 400 words) It will mostly be a report of occurrences, or recording of lyrics (probably including some actual recordings if I can manage to do something good) on the part of the SCP, and accounts of puzzled personel on the other part.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact the Choir is still a vastly unknown phenomenon, while being deeply sad (and emotions are good at hooking people, as they say)

Additional Notes: I'm really lost on the items numbers, despite reading about it I could use some help ! Also I don't remember reading about such a SCP, but if you did, feel free to tell me ! I'm really looking to make something new ! I want to reference beautiful stories to help people see past the many horror tales and get into SCPs too and also I also welcome any criticism ! I already have a Draft too (new member but long-time SCP reader)

item.title: Friendship bracelet seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous bracelet which removes the wearers ability to experience any and all negative emotions. This bracelet then compels its wearer to create "friendship bracelets" out of available materials and attempts to convince others to wear these bracelets. the original bracelet changes size in order to always fit its wearer, the other bracelets created by an affected person have all the same effects excluding this one.

Central Narrative: The story will be told through an interview log of an agent who was sent as part of a pair to investigate a quickly growing cult. The cult was in possession of the original bracelet and all of its members were wearing other instances. The agent will have been tortured, along with their partner dying to the torture, and was recovered along with the SCP when an MTF was deployed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is an exploration of the implications of a person (or group of people) having a single goal that consumes their life. This exploration is diversified by the individuals not having negative emotions (which lead to morals) to "hold them back".

item.title: Typowriter (Seeking Greenlight/Critiques or Edits)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Highly powerful reality bender manifesting in the form of a common typewriter. The typewriter will essentially create "transcripts" of nearby media, although it often makes typos. If a typo happens to create a sentence in the transcript that grammatically makes sense, it will become reality. It runs forever and will make increasingly more typos on a transcript if the same piece of media is shown to it multiple times.

Central Narrative: I plan for this to be an SCP that has been in containment for awhile, however without any reliable containment procedures. There will be an extensive list of research notes and observations about the operations of SCP XXXX. The main "narrative" stems from a recovered journal. The SCP is contained by singing up 4 unwitting rural towns to use their local news stations, newspapers, and radio broadcasts for SCP XXXX. Although MTFs patrol all 4 towns constantly, one woman begins to keep a journal of all the weird alterations that happen, so she can be sure she isn't going crazy (as the towns are frequently amnestizied due to the SCP)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Completely random reality bender that is able to warp anything by writing a typo

Additional Notes: The reality anchors do not work on this SCP, in actuality because it kills some of the fun associated with it. I think a decent theory within the narrative as to why this is so is that SCP XXXX is a recovered byproduct of SCP 3812 (SCP-3812)

item.title: Greenlight Concept - Article - Horror / History -Related to Sarkicism & CotBG
item.description: Seeking review of concept for an SCP article.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking review of concept for an SCP article. Tried this out about nine years ago, did bad, and want to give it another go having read a lot more of the material and matured as a writer/person.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror & History

Page Layout (Optional): Standard in-depth containment procedure, followed by a retrieval log and accompanied by a brief test log with two or three addenda related to the nature of the SCP. I don't want to perform anything out of the ordinary format-wise with it being my first entry, but a timeline of the SCP's apprehension by groups of interest may be relevant.

Elevator Pitch:

A forest-spirit/lesser goddess of creation and fertility that asexually births creatures based
upon what she consumes is captured by the Church of the Broken God, and turned into a weapon to convert organic material into inorganic material. They lose her, and she exchanges hands between organizations for hundreds of years before ending up in foundation custody totally unrecognizable to what she once was, with a sinister corruption of her godly ability.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:

Following the first war of the Flesh, Cyrus the Great founded a covenant to search the world for a new means to defeat the Sarkic threat. This group set out, with generations passing before eventually finding a minor fertility goddess unique in her ability to produce life asexually and rapidly by consuming organic matter. They captured her, but became indoctrinated by the Church of the Broken God over time, and augmented her heavily. She would eventually escape with the aid of a man enamored with her, and sire a child with him, the location of which is unknown but she is believed to be endowed with the same ability. Over time different organizations got ahold of the spirit and altered her repeatedly to suit their needs or designs with her now bordering on unrecognizable as herself.

Her modern iteration is a mess of added mechanical and organic apertures both internal and external that have removed her god-like beauty to some extent. Her mistreatment by mankind has jaded her to the point of being predatory, and resulted in her fractured psyche turning to exploitation and predation of mankind through producing her unique offspring. Organic material she consumed is now converted into mechanically augmented horrors when she births them, and vice versa.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

The indigenous American Coyote character escapes to his own metanarrative properties, and the Foundation seeks to stop him from spreading to other folklore.

Page Layout: Bog-standard SCP format

Elevator Pitch: The set of Indigenous American stories about Coyote are an anomalous set of living narrative and metanarrative characteristics, which the Foundation worries might "jump" into other contemporary narratives. "Coyote" fools the Foundation and involves the Chaos Insurgency

Central Narrative: There is definitely a plot to this, but I hope you'll find it interesting enough to warrant such a big explanation:

+ show block
– hide block

A culture's practices and beliefs determine its stories, right? But what if the stories start to have a mind (or agenda) of their own? A Foundation anthropologist reports that the set of stories about Coyote acts differently from any other set of stories about a character (indigenous or otherwise); specifically, the stories and the overall set itself shares Coyote's characteristics, as well as some instinct for self preservation and an unknown degree of sapience. This worries the Foundation, who are concerned about what would happen if Coyote discovers how to (or maybe just decides to) jump into other contemporary narrative-sets. They have no idea what will happen in that scenario.

A year later, Foundation web-sweeper bots detect a set of movie concepts, novel plots, and fanfiction arcs, many involving birds of some kind, which overall "behaved like a narrative animal, but with more personality", similarly to the Coyote set. The foundation at first classifies this as a new, similar SCP, but the anthropologist later realizes that it is in fact a containment breach, where "Coyote took the form of a bird". The site is taken down, and it is discovered that many of the original posts were made by the teenage daughter of a former member of the Chaos Insurgency of Kootenai descent.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Foundation deals with a metanarrative SCP and gets hoodwinked. The Chaos Insurgency gets involved.

Additional Notes: The most important thing I want to watch out for is that I don't mis-portray parts of any Native American culture(s). That being said, this very much isn't the mythical figure of Coyote as an SCP (that'd be both stupid and impossible to write), but is a conscious set of stories which act similar to the character they portray. The point is to look at how the foundation will handle an SCP like this, and vice versa…

item.content:encoded:

Genre: My design is meant to be spooky, but I may not achieve this factor.

Information is going to be structured in the following layout; Appearance description (Height, weight, colour and shape), Discovery (How the anomaly was contained), Abilities (What the anomaly can do, how it does it etc) and the Addendums (Stories about previously explained things).

Elevator Pitch: The basic premise is a tall, slender, arctic hunter with elongated shoulder growths and large elbows, glowing crimson eyes, capable of seeing infrared radiation and heat signatures. This is used as a hunting technique in the arctic weather.

+ show block
– hide block

The anomaly has thousands of tiny muscles on its skin capable of moving guanine crystals to adjust the wavelength of light being reflected off the skin of the anomaly. This is commonly known as camouflage, and is the same method that the Chamaeleonidae (Common Chameleon) uses. Bone marrow scans and nervous axon scans have suggested that overgrowths on the anomaly's shoulder blades and elbows contain many nerve endings, which transfer electrical signals in large amounts to a particular area which creates an electromagnetic field. These electromagnetic pulses disrupt nearby local electric signals. It may use this to alter the function of electrical signals in the brain, or to inhibit power of technology.

Central Narrative: The narrative for initial containment is the following: It was a normal day in the UK Arctic Research Facility. Cold, as usual, but the sacred electric heaters were keeping staff alive. It was collection day, where the scientific staff would take a collection of snow for carbon-testing, a process where the amount of carbon that is in a snowflake is collected to see the effects of the greenhouse effect. As the staff left the facility, the power went out. As the staff stumbled over to the generator, senior researcher Noel Leon noticed a small red glow. Must have been nothing. H got back to fixing the generator. The fuses had been replaced. They become brittle and break in the cold weather. But as soon as the generator start-up was initiated, the generator failed. What was going on? Suddenly, pat… pat… pat…. Something was behind him, but when he turned around, there was nothing but footprints. SNAP. The crunch of his bones in SCP-XXXX's mouth was horrifying, but unheard to remaining staff. As it entered the facility, seven of it's prey had already been frozen. An easy meal. Junior researcher Doctor Edward turned a corner, but the anomaly was gone, just a frozen, half-eaten corpse. item.content:encoded:
A book that when you write something on a page and plant the page, it will grow into a tree and fruit what was written on it.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Use of extensive test logs and interviews

Elevator Pitch: Its an old notebook with blank pages that when you write something on one of the pages and plant the page, a tree grows and will fruit what's written on it. The only limits is that what's written is that it must be a tangible item, the item is not fictitious, and the writer knows/"believes to have seen" what they're writing about. What's written is based on knowledge and assumptions of item. In the event that item written does not fruit, the a paper with the written word will fruit instead. The fruited item will be identical to what was written and based off the knowledge of the writer but will taste, smell, and decay like an apple. Pages are replenished when closing the book.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The book is found in an isolated arctic Russian town and brought to Foundation for research and further testing. As testing continues, more discoveries are made about the capabilities, loopholes, and uses of what the book produces from creating other fruits besides apples to inorganic objects to "cloning" sapient beings and SCPs. At that point, much backtracking is done with revelations such as: the aforementioned townspeople being creations of the book, finding the head researcher is a "clone" of themself, and that the book may not be the original one. Conclusion would be having it become a level 4 or 5 SCP after some O5 "cloning" or other Foundation disrupting incident.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Through test logs and interviews, the reader can watch the growing understanding of researchers what the book is capable of. The tone progresses from light-hearted to serious as additional discoveries are made. Its more narrative driven rather than input-output explorative, and would go into how certain things can be overlooked and how the scp is actually more dangerous because its in the foundation.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP and first work of creative writing that I have done in a very long time. I am unsure to how in-depth I should go with the test logs, whether this a creative enough concept, or if something like this already exists.

item.title: "God Bless Americana Anómalos" Idea Critique Request
item.description: The American Flag was a plant all along.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout:

  • ConProcs
  • Description
  • Discovery Log
  • List of SCP-Events
  • Testing Logs
  • Interview and Final Word from O5

Elevator Pitch:

You're home alone, watching the tv of your country. You hear a noise in the other room and go to investigate. You see nothing but the American flag planted firmly in the center of the room.

Then a voice whispers to you

"God bless America".

And then you start a revolution.

-Marcelles_Raynes 12/4/2020

1 out of every 5,000 American flags is a sentient petal of an extra-dimensional plant that symbiotically infects humans (mostly foreigners) and puppets them into influencing the political state of America with non-anomalous memetic strategies.

Story and Hook +
Story and Hook -

Central Narrative: The first American flag, the original progenitor of this SCP, inspired the American Revolution only because the east coast was the perfect habitat for it to grow. The anomaly successfully thrived in America for centuries undetected, keeping their percentage of American hosts lower than the percentage of non-American hosts globally. And while these flags are too light to stop the wind from pushing them around outside, inside the human body they can morph themselves into microscopic threads to navigate, manipulate their hosts, and avoid detection.

It isn’t until 2015, when the Bundy standoff between the BLM and the ATF revealed a new progenitor flag attempting to start another revolution, that the Foundation identifies the presence of the anomaly. While the Foundation realizes complete containment of the anomaly would force them and the US into open war, they also discover that the anomaly has been defending humanity from numerous shape-shifting anomalies in secret, making itself essential to their needs too. They accept that the anomaly cannot and does not need to be actively contained, so, with caution, they focus on the threat of wild American flags going rogue and starting a new America all over again.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Inspired by a comment made by Marcelles_Raynes 's perspective on the phrase “God Bless America,” this SCP focuses on highlighting and mocking much of American flavored jingoism while not explaining it all off as something completely unnatural.

Johnny Appleseed, tea dumping in the Boston river, the start of the Spanish-American war, Westerns, and others are given are both humorous and unsettling examples. Test logs show how flags choose/infect their host and how infected hosts take down other shape-shifting threats (hint: think of a "pulling a handkerchief out of the mouth" magic trick but deadly.) Also hints at the end about what might have O5 worried most of all about the anomalies freedom.

Additional Notes: The title is supposed to be the genus and species name but correct me if I got the order or idea wrong. Thanks!
